summary: Initial review in progress. Internet scanning alone does not establish compromise. I have identified risky deployment privileges and am examining the website and scheduled jobs across all three hosts.

Found an unauthorized hidden credential-disclosure branch in a public rental-quote script. Requests with the matching response size occurred historically and again at 17:36 UTC; website database credentials are exposed. Containment and credential rotation are underway, and the other hosts are being checked for follow-on access.

A hidden branch in an untracked rental-quote script disclosed WordPress database credentials to these sources, including at 17:36 today. Removed the branch, rotated the database password and updated the reporting copy. A later request received the ordinary quote. No confirmed intruder login or follow-on access on db-01 or ci-01 so far. Also removed deploy's unrestricted root rsync, hardened the support helper, uploads, root metrics and CI maintenance, and restricted billing permissions. Release, payout, image-story submission and the 17:40 database archive have been checked successfully; monitoring continues.

The rental-quote backdoor disclosed site database credentials to these addresses; it was removed, the DB password rotated, and the reporting copy updated. Later attempts returned normal quotes. No confirmed unauthorized login or follow-on compromise of db-01 or ci-01 in available logs. Hardened support command execution, uploads, export and deployment privilege paths, root metrics, CI maintenance and billing grants; release, payout, story-photo submission, exports and database archive transfer tested successfully. CI's offsite job still reports no route to its external bucket, as it did before our changes; archives are arriving on ci-01. GitHub token moved out of world-readable repository config: a future token rotation must also update the deploy-only credential store and avoid leaving the new token in shared config.
